cards.b: The ability to cope with (or meet) the demands of the environment.
Ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen to muscles for long periods.
Ability of a muscle or group to contract repeatedly without tiring.
Maximum force a muscle can exert in one contraction.
Changing direction quickly while keeping control.
Static: staying balanced while still. Dynamic: balance while moving.
The time between a stimulus and the start of the response.
Cardiovascular endurance: 20 m shuttle runs to bleeps getting faster; level reached is recorded.
Flexibility: reach forward along a ruler with straight legs; distance in cm.
Power: difference in cm between standing reach and jump height.
Reaction time: catch a dropped ruler; the distance caught is measured.
Static balance: stand on one leg with heel raised; time until balance is lost.
Strengths and weaknesses, monitor improvement, compare to others, plan training, motivation, suitability.
Maximum volume of oxygen the body can take in, transport and use per minute; measure of cardiovascular endurance.

short.q: Describe how to carry out the Sit and Reach Test.
short.model: Sit with straight legs and feet against the box. Reach forward slowly as far as possible, hold for two seconds and record the distance in cm.
points: Reach forward slowly and record the distance

short.q: Which fitness components are most important for a goalkeeper? Justify your answer.
short.model: Reaction time to respond to shots and agility to move quickly to save the ball; also power to dive.

short.q: Explain what is meant by VO₂ max.
short.model: The maximum volume of oxygen the body can take in, transport and use per minute during exercise; a high value means better cardiovascular endurance.
points: Maximum oxygen taken in and used

short.q: A player's 30 m sprint time falls from 4.8 s to 4.5 s. What does this show and why was it tested?
short.model: It shows her speed has improved by 0.3 s so training worked; tests monitor improvement and show strengths and weaknesses.

short.q: State two factors that affect VO₂ max, with a reason for each.
short.model: Age: it falls as the heart and lungs work less well. Training: aerobic training improves oxygen delivery and use.
